questions.question: Why laboratory equipment safety is important? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Why laboratory equipment safety is important?
  • Proper use of laboratory equipment helps avoid burns, cuts, electric shocks, and chemical spills that can cause serious
  • harm to students and staff. Safe handling prevents breakage or malfunction of expensive and delicate instruments,
  • ensuring they remain i n good working condition for future use. Following safety procedures avoids contamination
  • and errors during experiments, leading to correct and dependable scientific results. Safety practices promote
  • discipline, cleanliness, and responsibility, creating a secure environment for effective learning and research.
  • [Any 3 relevant points- Give 4 Mark]

questions.question: Explain why glassware is preferred in laboratory experiments compared to other materials. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain why glassware is preferred in laboratory experiments compared to other materials
  • Glassware is preferred in laboratory experimen ts because it possesses several important properties that make it
  • suitable for accurate and safe scientific work . Glass does not react with most acids, bases, or solvents, ensuring that
  • experiments are not contaminated b y reactions with the container. It can withstand high and low temperatures,
  • allowing it to be used for heating, cooling, or boiling substances.
  • The clear nature of glass allows easy observation of reactions, color changes, and measurements. Glass can be easily
  • sterilized and reused without affecting experimental results. Prevents absorption of chemicals, maintaining purity of
  • substances used.
  • [Any 3 relevant points related to this answer give 4 Mark]

questions.question: Why must oxidizing and reducing agents be stored separately? Illustrate with an example / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Why must oxidizing and reducing agents be stored separately? Illustrate with an example?
  • Oxidizing and reducing agents must be stored separately because they can react violently with each other, often
  • causing fire, explosion, or release of toxic gases even without any external ignition source. Eg. Potassium Permaganate
  • is a strong oxidizing agent and Glycerol a reducing agent. If these two come in contact, they ignite spontaneously due
  • to an intense redox reaction. Immediate combustion without any spark or flame.
  • [Give full credit to reasonable Explanation-3.5 mark and any one example 3.5 Mark]

questions.question: Give a short essay on safe work procedures for handling hazardous chemicals. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Give a short essay on safe work procedures for handling hazardous chemicals.
  • All chemical containers must be clearly labeled with the chemical name, concentration, hazard symbols, and date of
  • preparation. Use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) [gloves, goggles, lab coats, face shield and respirators. Fume
  • hoods are necessary to prevent inhalation of toxic vapors or dust. Chemicals must be stored separately according to
  • their properties —for example, oxidizing and reducing agents, acids and bases, should not be kept together and
  • Flammable substances must be kept away from open fla mes or heat sources. Chemicals must be handled with clean,
  • dry hands and appropriate tools such as tongs or pipettes. Spills should be cleaned immediately using proper
  • neutralizing agents. Chemical waste must be disposed of according to approved procedures , never poured into sinks
  • or drains. Safety equipment such as fire extinguishers, eye wash stations, and safety showers should be easily
  • accessible. Workers must be trained to respond quickly in case of spills, fires, or chemical exposure
  • [Any Reasonable five points - Give full credit]

questions.question: Compare the functions of respirators and masks in providing safety to laboratory workers. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Compare the functions of respirators and masks in providing safety to laboratory workers
  • Respirators protect the wearer from inhaling hazardous substances like chemicals, dust, and biological agents. Masks
  • mainly prevent the spread of droplets from the wearer to the environment. Respirators provide a tight seal around
  • the face for maximum protection. Masks fit loosely and offer limited filtration. Respirators use filters or cartridges
  • to remove harmful particles and gases. Masks are suitable for basic hygiene and low-risk environments. Respirators
  • require maintenance and proper fitting, while masks are usually disposable or washable for simple use .[Any three
  • comparison give 7 marks]

questions.question: Explain the importance of using hazard pictograms in chemical labeling, with examples. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the importance of using hazard pictograms in chemical labeling, with examples
  • a)Immediate Hazard Recognition: Pictograms allow anyone handling a chemical —scientists, students, or workers—
  • to instantly recognize potential hazards without needing to read detailed text b)Supports Safe Handling and Storage:
  • Each pictogram indicates specific precautions (e.g., wear gloves, avoid inhalation, use fume hood).c)Prevents Health
  • Hazards: Some hazards (like carcinogenicity or respiratory sensitization) are not immediately visible. Pictograms alert
  • users even when the danger isn’t obvious.d) Legal and Regulatory Compliance: Use of correct pictograms is required
  • by law under systems like OSHA Hazard Communication Standard (HCS) e)Universal Understanding -
  • Pictograms are language-independent, ensuring that people from different linguistic backgrounds can recognize the
  • same hazard.
  • Pictogram Symbol Example Substance Hazard Type
  • Skull and Crossbones Acute toxicity Sodium cyanide Poisonous
  • Flame Flammable Ethanol Fire hazard
  • Corrosion Corrosive Sulfuric acid Burns metals/skin
  • Exploding Bomb Explosive TNT Explosion hazard
  • Health Hazard (silhouette with star) Chronic health hazard Benzene Carcinogenic
  • Exclamation Mark Irritant Ammonia solution Causes irritation
  • Environment Environmental hazard Pesticides Toxic to aquatic life
  • Over Circle Oxidizer Hydrogen peroxide Intensifies fire
  • Gas Cylinder Gas under pressure Propane Compressed gas risk

questions.question: How do we respond to chemical spill? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• How do we respond to chemical spill?
  • Immediately inform others nearby and, if the spill is large or involves toxic fumes, evacuate the area. Identify the type
  • and quantity of chemical spilled. Only trained personnel should handle hazardous or unknown chemicals. Wear
  • appropriate gloves, goggles, lab coat, and mask before attempting cleanup to avoid contact or inhalation. Avoid letting
  • the chemical enter drains. Neutralize acids or bases if possible (e.g., use sodium bicarbonate for acid spills). Collect
  • the waste in a labeled disposal container. Wash the area thoroughly with water or suitable cleaning agents and ensure
  • good ventilation to remove fumes. Notify the safety offic er or supervisor and record the spill details for future
  • prevention. [Any reasonable 5 points - Give full credit]

questions.question: Explain the significance of waste containers in maintaining safety during laboratory and industrial waste disposal. / [CO2] [7x5 = 35]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the significance of waste containers in maintaining safety during laboratory and industrial waste
  • disposal.
  • Waste containers play a vital role in ensuring safety during the handling, storage, and disposal of waste generated
  • in laboratories and industries.. The following points explain their significance:1. Segregation of Waste: Different
  • types of waste—chemical, biological, radioactive, and general—must be kept separate to prevent dangerous chemical
  • reactions or contamination. 2. Containment of Hazardous Materials: Waste containers are designed to safely hold
  • hazardous materials, preventing leaks, spills, and the release of toxic vapors. 3.Prevention of Accidents and Injuries:
  • Using proper containers —such as sharps containers for needles and broken glass —prevents injuries and infections
  • caused by accidental contact with sharp or contaminated objects.4. Environmental Protection: Secure waste
  • containers prevent the release of harmful chemicals and biological agents into air, soil, or water, thereby protecting
  • the ecosystem from pollution and contamination.5. Compliance with Regulations: Proper labeling, storage, and
  • disposal using approved waste containers ensure compliance with environmental, health, and safety regulations set
  • by authorities. 6.Ease of Handling and Transport: Well-designed containers make it easier to store, transport, and
  • dispose of waste safely.7. Minimization of Cross-Contamination: Keeping waste in designated containers reduces
  • the risk of cross -contamination between hazardous and non -hazardous materials. (Any 5 Reasonable points- Give
  • Full Mark)

questions.question: What systemic failures led to the Bhopal Gas Disaster, and how can the lessons learned be applied to enhance modern industrial safety and accountability? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What systemic failures led to the Bhopal Gas Disaster, and how can the lessons learned be applied to
  • enhance modern industrial safety and accountability?
  • Safety systems were not properly maintained. The refrigeration unit (to keep MIC below 5°C) was shut down to
  • save money. Safety devices (Gas Scrubber, alarm system) not working .Over-storage of MIC. No proper
  • containment system or emergency vent to control gas leaks.
  • Modern industrial safety and accountability
  • The Bhopal tragedy taught the world that safety, transparency, and accountability must come before profit. Regular
  • monitoring, trained personnel, and strict enforcement of safety standards are essential to prevent such disasters.
  • Enforce strong laws for hazardous industries. Regular inspection and monitoring by safety authorities.
  • Ensure all safety devices (alarms, scrubbers, flare towers, etc.) are working and regularly checked . Prevent cost-
  • cutting at the expense of safety. Workers must receive proper training to handle dangerous chemicals. Regular
  • safety drills and emergency response training should be mandatory. Companies must share information about
  • hazardous materials and risks with employees and local authorities. Maintain clear labeling and documentation of
  • chemicals. Every plant should have a disaster management plan and emergency evacuation system. Hospitals and
  • local bodies should be trained to respond to chemical accidents. Hazardous industries should be built away from
  • residential areas. Companies must be legally responsible for safety failures. Install automatic monitoring systems
  • and real-time leak detectors to identify hazards early. (Reasonable Explanation for systemic failures (4 points)-7.5
  • marks and reasonable explanation for lessons learned (4 points) -7.5 marks)

questions.question: Explain the significance of Hazard (H) and Precautionary (P) statements in chemical safety / [CO2] [15x1 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the significance of Hazard (H) and Precautionary (P) statements in chemical safety
  • Hazard statement is assigned a code beginning with “H” followed by three digits (e.g., H200, H315, H400). First
  • number designating the type of hazard as follows:"2" for physical hazards,"3" for health hazards,"4" for environmental
  • hazards.
  • Significance: 1 .Describe the type and severity of chemical hazards: H-statements clearly indicate whether a
  • chemical is flammable, toxic, corrosive, carcinogenic, or environmentally harmful.2. Facilitate quick risk
  • assessment: Standardized codes (e.g., H225 – highly flammable liquid and vapor) help workers identify risks
  • immediately.3. Promote consistent communication: Globally recognized wording reduces confusion across
  • different languages and regions.4. Guide safe handling and storage: Knowledge of hazard s allows selection of
  • appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) and preventive measures.
  • Precautionary Statements (P -codes): Precautionary statements describe recommended measures to minimize or
  • prevent adverse effects from exposure, improper handling, or storage of chemicals. Its main purpose is to provide
  • practical safety advice for users — how to protect themselves and the environment. Each precautionary statement is
  • assigned a code beginning with “P” followed by three digits (e.g., P102, P280, P301).
  • Significance: 1.Provide instructions for safety measures: P-statements advise on prevention, response, storage,
  • and disposal of chemicals.2. Reduce accidents and exposure: For example, P210: Keep away from heat/sparks/open
  • flames.3.Ensure emergency preparedness: Statements provide steps for first aid, spill response, and containment.4.
  • Support regulatory compliance: Following P -statements aligns with occupational safety and environmental
  • regulations. (Explanation for Hazard (H) (4 points) – 7.5 marks and Precautionary (P) (4 points) - 7.5 marks)
  • ______________________
